Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A mostly sunny thermal day with peak site w* up to 496 ft/min and no precipitation. Sharp lapse rates (>8 °C/km at several sites) will produce strong, turbulent thermals requiring advanced pilot skills. Wind directions are mixed: Slide Mountain, Rainbow Ridge, and Duck Hill (afternoon) offer favorable alignment, while Daydreams is unflyable due to weak lift and hazardous shear.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — SE wind outside preferred ridge-soaring direction, but thermals usable. Window: 10am–3pm. Peak w* 378 fpm, thermal ceiling 2921 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 8.1 — advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Marginal — Brief window 9am–11am with NW winds suitable for ridge soaring; thermals build by 11am but wind then shifts SE. Peak w* 353 fpm, ceiling 3325 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 9.1 — advanced pilots only.
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable — Light winds within preferred 101±79° all day, consistent thermals. Window: 8am–4pm. Peak w* 364 fpm, thermal ceiling 2128 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Favorable — Strong thermals; wind favorable until 12pm, then light NE crosswind manageable. Window: 10am–4pm. Peak w* 496 fpm, ceiling 4520 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 8.4 — advanced pilots only.
  • West McClellan: Marginal — Wind direction E to NE unfavorable for W/SW launches, but light morning winds may permit; afternoon wind increases to 7 mph tailwind. Window: 11am–4pm. Peak w* 433 fpm, ceiling 3524 ft AGL.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — Persistent E wind 6–9 mph cross to S/SW launches; moderate thermals. Window: 10am–3pm. Peak w* 372 fpm, ceiling 2386 ft AGL.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — Excellent wind alignment (E/NE within 67±45°) and strong thermals. Window: 10am–4pm. Peak w* 483 fpm, ceiling 4550 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 9.2 — advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — Afternoon wind shifts to NW-N (within 340±70°) coinciding with strong thermals. Window: 12pm–6pm. Peak w* 458 fpm, ceiling 4377 ft AGL. Sharp lapse rate 9.3 — advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — Very weak thermals (peak w* 133 fpm), high bulk shear 18 mph, hazardous speed shear 5 mph, and persistent SE/E wind outside preferred 225±30°. Not flyable.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals: Sites with lapse rate >8 °C/km (Kingsbury 8.1, Hallelujah 9.1, McClellan 8.4, Rainbow 9.2, Duck Hill 9.3) will produce strong, turbulent thermals — suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.
  • Low-level wind shear: Hazardous speed shear at Daydreams (5 mph at 767 ft AGL) and Duck Hill (6 mph at 4,901 ft AGL). Hazardous directional shear at Hallelujah (38° layer change).
  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Possible downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines given regional flow and varying wind directions.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
